text:
Miriam: Quick question — can we add a token-level breakdown for TTFT vs decode in the performance dashboard? We need kernel-level attribution (cuBLAS vs fused-attn vs generic_matmul) per-route. Spotting regressions is hard now.

Sam: Yep, I'm on it. Thinking metric names: `infra.token_ttft_ms`, `infra.token_decode_ms`, `infra.kernel_ms_total` and `infra.kernel_count` with tags for `kernel`, `model`, `route`. Confirm tagging strategy?

Miriam: That sounds right. Also include `kv_cache_status` (hit/miss/partial) — decode for cache-hit should be much lower and we want that split in the waterfall.

Priya: Agree — add `cache_status` tag and `batch_size` tag. Batching heuristics change distribution a lot; we should bucket batch sizes (1,2-4,5-16,16+).

Josh: FYI when I added kernel attribution locally I spotted a perf regression on 7B-v2: kernel selector fell back to `generic_matmul` for seqLen>2048. Logs:
```
2026-01-11T09:12:03Z kernel_selector INFO model=7b-v2 seq_len=2300 selected=generic_matmul reason="no_fused_for_seqlen"
2026-01-11T09:12:03Z perf PROFILER kernel_time_ms=12.8 kernel=generic_matmul tokens=512
```
That fallback explains the spike in decode token ms.

Sam: Oof. That fallback would blow up `token_decode_ms`. Can you paste the profiler extract (p50/p95/p99)? We should feed those into the dashboard panels.

Josh: Profiler snippet from devbox:
```
# promql example to get per-kernel avg ms
sum by(kernel) (increase(infra.kernel_ms_total[5m])) / sum by(kernel) (increase(infra.kernel_count[5m]))
# sample output: fused_attn=2.1ms, cublas_gemm=3.0ms, generic_matmul=12.4ms
```

Priya: Dashboard panel suggestions: token TTFT waterfall (queue_delay + kernel + decode + emit), kernel heatmap by `model` and `seq_len_bucket`, per-route p50/p95/p99 for `token_decode_ms`, KV cache hit-rate panel, and a batch_size distribution panel.

Miriam: Also we need an automated regression alert: >15% increase in p95 `token_decode_ms` for any `route` within 24h. Perf-bot should post alerts to #incidents and include links to the kernel heatmap. :rotating_light:

perf-bot: Alert created: `token-decode-p95-regression`. Threshold=15% over 24h. Notified=#incidents.

Sam: I'm going to add the metrics and wire up the panels. Quick config change found: kernel selector priority reversed for some model families — patch below.
```
- selectors:
-  - name: fused_attn
-    priority: 10
-  - name: cublas_gemm
-    priority: 9
+ selectors:
+  - name: fused_attn
+    priority: 20
+  - name: cublas_gemm
+    priority: 19
```
Applying that fixed the fallback locally.

Josh: After the fix, quick numbers on seqLen=2048 test: p95 `token_decode_ms` dropped from ~45ms -> ~28ms on 7B-v2. KV hit tests show ~3-5x reduction when `cache_status=hit`.

Miriam: Nice. Once dashboards land, can we add drilldowns: click p95 -> open trace with per-token kernel attribution + batching info. Link to draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/token-latency-draft (private).

Sam: Will include trace links and example PromQL panels. Plan to canary the dashboard + selector patch next week.

Priya: Also — do we need to re-run full evals for output quality? Changing batching/selector could affect prompt scheduling and truncation behavior.

Miriam: Good point. Add evaluation run to the release checklist and gate the rollout on no regressions in our eval suite.

Josh: Also proposing a small `perf_health` metric per-route that combines p95_token_decode, kv_hit_rate, and queue_saturation so SRE can get a single health color.

Miriam: Love that. Add to next sprint. Thanks folks. :party_parrot:
